title: PPWR packaging compliance for small UK brands and exporters

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: A dated EU duty with market-access consequences; severity credible, frequency periodic rather than frequent.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Buyer defined (small UK brands/importers) but budget is inferred from vendor pricing only (vendor claims are weak secondary); capped at 2.

evidence_strength.rationale: Primary regulation/government sources plus multiple dated vendor pages establish the duty and a populated market.

distribution.rationale: Fragmented small-brand buyer with only plausible referral channels; no non-paid route evidenced (capped at 2).

differentiation.rationale: Direct overlap with several live vendors including a UK £49/mo tier; the feature set is the category standard.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A price test with small brands would be cheap and fast, though the wedge fail makes it unjustified.

feasibility.rationale: Buildable, but ~30 delegated/implementing acts remain pending, so maintaining correctness is a real burden.

economics.rationale: Modelled only and untested (capped at 2); a UK incumbent at £49/mo anchors price below a sustainable micro-tool margin.

founder_fit.rationale: Inferred fit for a packaging/regulatory domain expert; no owner-specific evidence.

risk.rationale: Regulatory detail is still changing and a wrong DoC has legal consequences; compliance-liability risk is material.

economic_buyer.note: Brands/importers are identifiable, but evidence they budget for a dedicated tool is vendor pricing only (weak secondary).
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Test whether small UK brands/importers already pay for PPWR tooling and at what price.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Legal exposure is credible but not evidenced as buyer pain or an existing line item for this segment.
painful_frequent_or_budgeted.resolve_via: Interview importers about current compliance spend and pain.

non_paid_distribution.note: Compliance-scheme/accountant referrals are plausible, not evidenced.

defensible_wedge.note: Multiple credible providers already sell PPWR compliance software, including a UK-branded £49/mo tier; the proposition is a feature of an established compliance-software category.

no_network_effects_needed.note: No obvious network effect, but not explicitly assessed.

plausible_margins.note: No cost model; incumbent price anchoring is a warning.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Model content-maintenance cost against a tested price.

acceptable_risk.note: Giving compliance advice carries liability; disclaimers and scope would need review.
acceptable_risk.resolve_via: Legal review of scope before any build.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A cheap test is conceivable but was not specified because the wedge already fails.

not_all_optimistic.note: Viability would require winning a fragmented segment against incumbents at a price they already set.
